reproduction_target: The computational half of the paper: basecalling of ONT direct-RNA POD5 signal, alignment/read-length-and-quality analysis, transcriptome assembly and isoform classification, and the derived comparisons between uMRT-based and Induro-based DRS libraries (Figures 3-5, Supplementary Tables 1-2). The molecular-biology optimisation (RT reactions, library prep, sequencing runs, RT-PCR validation) is wet-lab and out of scope (OOS, counted in W).
granularity_note: Coarse step list built from the 'Direct RNA Sequencing Data Analysis' Methods subsections (Basecalling; Mapping and read length analysis; Transcriptome and isoform analysis) plus the Code Availability list. One step per named tool/analysis invocation. Stage-1 prose-only: no workflow source, no config files, no parameter files were read; env_capture_class is 'n/a' for every step by protocol and the top verdict is capped at RI.

steps.label: Basecalling of raw POD5 to FASTQ - Dorado (v.7.8.3) via ONT MinKNOW, RNA004 4kHz chemistry, super-accurate basecalling (>= Q10), v5.1.0-130bps model
Alignment of total reads per sample to human genome GRCh38.p14 - EPI2ME alignment workflow (v1.2.4) with minimap2 (v2.28)
Combination of FASTQ files for replicate UHRR and Human Brain sequencing runs - OmicsBox (v3.5), commercial closed-source platform (biobam.com)
Down-sampling of combined uMRT Human Brain reads from 6.59M to 5.73M - SEQTK (v1.3-r106)
Read length and quality analysis for all samples - EPI2ME alignment workflow (v1.2.4), NanoPlot (v1.46.1), LongQC (v1.2)
Mapped read count per million (CPM) computed from NanoPlot binned read lengths - no script or notebook deposited
Mapped gene body coverage plots and read-quality-by-length plots for combined UHRR and Human Brain samples - RSeQC (v5.0.1)
Transcriptome assembly from combined replicate FASTQ - EPI2ME transcriptome workflow (v1.7.1), mapped to GRCh38.p14 with GENCODE v47 annotations via minimap2 (v2.28)
Transcript model generation - IsoQuant (v3.6.2) on GRCh38.p14 + GENCODE v47
Isoform characterization/classification of IsoQuant models against GENCODE - SQANTI3 (v3.5.2) with additional reference TSS annotation and PolyA motif files taken from the SQANTI3 GitHub repository

Manual IGV (v2.19.6) inspection of the longest reads underlying the 10 longest Human Brain transcripts (group by strand, sort by aligned read length, select longest continuous same-strand read) on BAM/index files from the EPI2ME transcriptome workflow
RNA sources and poly(A) RNA preparation (Universal Human Reference RNA, human brain RNA)
Reverse transcription condition comparison - Induro RT at 60C vs UltraMarathonRT (uMRT) at 30C, including RNA hydrolysis assays
ONT direct RNA sequencing library preparation (adapter ligation, clean-up, optimisation of ancillary molecular-biology steps)
Nanopore sequencing runs (RNA004 4kHz chemistry, run to ~3-3.5 million reads over 48-72 h)
RT-PCR validation of selected transcripts (primers in Supplementary Table 3)

headline.static_readiness: 0/11 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification). Under-claims by construction: Tier-1 prose-only cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency, and this paper links only third-party tool repositories, so no author-side environment capture could be inspected.
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 8/11 (72.7%) readiness upper bound (n_R-star + n_RI)/|S| - 'ready for a reproduction attempt', never 'reproducible'. The three NI steps are OmicsBox FASTQ merging (proprietary), the CPM derivation (no script), and the RSeQC coverage plots (no gene-model reference stated).
headline.coverage: computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 11/16 (68.8%); 5 wet-lab steps are OOS and excluded from the denominator

gaps.missing: No author-authored analysis repository. The Code Availability section lists only third-party tool homepages: EPI2ME wf-alignment, EPI2ME wf-transcriptomes, SQANTI3, OmicsBox. No parameter files, no workflow config, no scripts for the derived quantities (CPM, percent-difference, figure generation) are deposited or linked.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the actual EPI2ME/IsoQuant/SQANTI3 invocation configs and the plotting/derivation scripts in a versioned repository (tagged release or Zenodo DOI) and cite it.

gaps.where: Methods - Mapping and read length analysis (step C3)
gaps.missing: Replicate FASTQ combination was performed in OmicsBox (v3.5), a commercial closed-source platform (biobam.com). The exact operation is not reproducible without a licence, and no equivalent open command is given.
gaps.how_to_close: State the equivalent open-source operation (e.g. concatenation order and command) or provide the merged FASTQ as a deposited intermediate.

gaps.missing: Only a BioProject accession (PRJNA1378338) is given. There is no per-sample / per-run mapping from library (uMRT vs Induro; UHRR vs Human Brain; replicate 1 vs 2) to SRA run accession, so the specific FASTQ inputs of each analysis step cannot be identified from the paper alone.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a sample-to-run accession table mapping each figure panel's input to an SRR/BioSample id.

gaps.where: Methods - 'Mapped read count per million (CPM) was calculated using the number of binned read lengths generated by NanoPlot' (step C6)
gaps.missing: The binning scheme and the CPM normalisation code are not provided; no script accompanies the derivation.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the derivation script/notebook including bin edges and normalisation denominator.

gaps.where: Methods - SQANTI3 (v3.5.2) 'using additional reference TSS annotation and PolyA motif files supplied in the GitHub repository' (step C10); also the CAGE data used for 5' support
gaps.missing: The reference TSS/CAGE and polyA-motif resource files are pulled from a GitHub repository with no commit, tag, or release pinned - a prose-only, out-of-band reference-resource reference. The GENCODE v47 and GRCh38.p14 references are named but no download URL/checksum is given.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the SQANTI3 commit/tag used and record checksums or versioned URLs for the TSS/CAGE, polyA-motif, GENCODE v47 and GRCh38.p14 files. Stage-2 code inspection is required to assign env_capture_class A/B/C.

gaps.where: Methods - down-sampling with SEQTK v1.3-r106 (step C4)
gaps.missing: seqtk sampling is pseudorandom; no random seed is reported, so the exact 5.73M-read subset cannot be regenerated. Scoring is capped at distributional match.
gaps.how_to_close: Report the seed used, or deposit the down-sampled read-id list / FASTQ.

gaps.where: (gap subtype 2a - versions stated, parameters not) Methods - EPI2ME workflows (C2, C5, C8), RSeQC (C7), IGV (C11)
gaps.missing: Tool versions are pinned in prose, but the parameter sets are not. No command lines, no minimap2 preset/args, no EPI2ME workflow parameter file, no RSeQC gene-model BED, no IsoQuant data-type/model settings. Container tags or Nextflow revisions used to run the EPI2ME workflows are not stated.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish full command lines / Nextflow -params-file and -r revision for each workflow invocation.

gaps.missing: Basecalling was run through ONT MinKNOW on the sequencing instrument; the run environment (MinKNOW version, GPU/host configuration) is device-bound and not described. Raw POD5 signal files are the input, but the Data Availability statement says only 'sequencing data', and SRA deposition of raw POD5 is not explicitly stated - so the basecalling step may not be re-runnable from public inputs.
gaps.how_to_close: State the MinKNOW version and confirm whether POD5 raw signal is deposited (and where); otherwise declare the basecalled FASTQ as the reproduction entry point.

gaps.missing: Selection of 'the longest continuous read within the pool of same-strand aligned reads' is a manual, operator-judgement GUI procedure with no script; the 10-longest-transcript selection is externalised to the EPI2ME transcriptome workflow output without a stated tie-breaking or filtering rule.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide a script that performs the same selection from the BAM, or deposit the selected read ids.
